reason: Short-lived radionuclides can heat rocky planetesimals, a plausible first step toward separating their interiors.
expectation: The rocky bodies should heat internally, potentially melting and separating their materials.

effect: The rocky planetesimal has melted, making separation of its materials the likely next step.
reaction: The qualification that not all asteroids melt makes the outcome more informative.
reason: Gravity should help dense metal sink through the molten rocky body.
expectation: The body should differentiate into metal-rich and rocky regions.

effect: The body has differentiated, and its rocky layers need to cool before collisions can expose fragments.
reaction: The distinction between separation and subsequent solidification is useful.
reason: Escaping radiation should cool and solidify the layered planetesimal.
expectation: The outer rocky layers should solidify, preparing the body to be broken apart.

effect: The asteroid’s outer rock has solidified, so a collision can now break apart its differentiated layers.
reaction: The cooling step makes the sequence physically clearer.
reason: Collisions between small bodies should expose fragments of the asteroid’s rock and metal.
expectation: The collision should break the asteroid and expose stone and metal from its interior.

effect: The collision completed the goal of exposing stone and metal; the remaining goal concerns water in altered rock.
reaction: The rocky fragments show how collisions reveal a body's internal layers.
reason: Heating an icy planetesimal may melt its ice and allow water to interact with rock.
expectation: The icy body should warm internally, possibly producing liquid water.

effect: Internal heating produced liquid water inside the icy body, setting up a water–rock reaction.
reaction: A frozen exterior concealing liquid water is a useful contrast.
reason: Silicate grains provide rock for the liquid water to alter.

choice.combine: Liquid water inside an icy body

expectation: Water should react with the silicate material, incorporating water into altered rock.

effect: The water–silicate reaction formed hydrated asteroid rock and completed the remaining goal, showing how rock can carry hydrogen even after exposed ice is gone.
reaction: That connection between internal water and hydrated rock was a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making water-bearing asteroid rock was most worthwhile: it connected hidden liquid water to a possible contribution to Earth’s volatile inventory.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cooling the differentiated asteroid was straightforward, though it clarified why solid fragments could later be broken off.

surprise.text: I was struck that a frozen-looking body could contain liquid water and produce hydrated rock inside.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the combinations followed the physical sequence described in the results.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how these differentiated fragments and water-bearing rocks contribute to the growing Earth; the chapter made those processes understandable.
